I am 66 years old, and I have worked this land for half a century. My father taught me to farm before I ever went to school — not that I ever did — and I have watched this soil through good years and bad. My farm is 14.5 mu, just enough for two people to manage if we are smart about labor. I plant winter wheat after the autumn maize comes off, and then maize again the moment the wheat is harvested in early June. That is the only way to squeeze two crops from one piece of ground in Quzhou.

This year, I will plough the maize stubble under before I sow wheat in mid-October. I trust ploughing for wheat because it buries the residue and opens the soil deep. I will sow an improved wheat variety from the seed station — not the old local landrace, because the new ones resist lodging better. I will spread compound fertilizer as a base dose and top-dress urea at jointing when the wheat turns a little pale. I will irrigate four times: the overwintering water to protect the seedlings from the dry cold, the green-up water in March, the jointing water in April, and one more at grain filling in May. Water is the one thing I do not gamble on, because I have my well. I will spray twice for weeds and bugs, once in early spring and again only if I see disease moving in.

For maize, the window after wheat harvest is narrow, so I will run the rotary tiller to prepare the seedbed quickly and plant hybrid maize seed the same day. Hybrid seed costs more, but I learned long ago that it pays for itself. I will band compound fertilizer with the seed and side-dress nitrogen at the big trumpet stage. Maize drinks less than wheat, and summer brings some rain, so I will irrigate twice — once when the tassels appear, and once at grain filling if the August heat is fierce. Two sprays: a pre-emergence herbicide and one insecticide if the armyworms arrive. At my age, with only my wife and me, I cannot afford unnecessary work. I expect my wheat to yield around 450 kg per mu, and the maize about 550 kg per mu, assuming the weather does not turn cruel.
